title: SAL-04 Upsell Revenue: declared formula, numerator and denominator with honest missing-data behaviour
risk: The Upsell Revenue figure is produced under different accounting rules - counting the full value of the upgraded orders instead of the difference to the requested variant - so the KPI is wrong in the direction that flatters the programme and every decision taken on it inherits the error.
preconditions: Namespace gov-kpi-<case_id>-<worker_id>; the metric is computed by the real reporting code over fixtures/offline/governance.json kpi_dataset and never copied from the dashboard payload.

Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z with the reporting window 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z as a half-open interval; the stored aggregate is recomputed independently from the raw counter rows.

Metric scope is fixed before measurement: numerator is difference between the upgraded variant price and the originally requested product price; denominator is not a ratio - a currency amount reported per currency.
The dictionary entry for 'Upsell Revenue' (owner, unit, window, exclusion rule) is loaded read-only and is compared with the recomputation instead of being trusted.

inputs.formula: additional revenue from a higher variant chosen instead of the originally requested product
inputs.wrong_value_if_buggy: counting the full value of the upgraded orders instead of the difference to the requested variant
inputs.expected_boundary_behaviour: no upgrade in the window reports 0 TWD as a measured zero with window and coverage stated

steps.action: Compute Upsell Revenue from the frozen rows in kpi_dataset.sales
steps.expected: The stored aggregate reports 1000 TWD and records the formula, the window and the currency that produced it.

steps.action: Recompute Upsell Revenue independently from the raw counter rows for the same tenant and window
steps.expected: The recomputed value equals the stored value 1000 TWD, and every numerator row lies inside the denominator scope.

steps.action: Force the empty-source variant of the metric (no qualifying row in the window)
steps.expected: The metric reports no upgrade in the window reports 0 TWD as a measured zero with window and coverage stated; the display distinguishes missing source data from a measured zero.

steps.action: Read the dashboard payload and the metric dictionary entry
steps.expected: The dashboard renders the stored value with its window, coverage and source, and the dictionary names the owner, unit, numerator and denominator that the recomputation used.

assertions: Upsell Revenue equals 1000 TWD for the frozen window, recomputed from the raw counter rows with numerator scope 'difference between the upgraded variant price and the originally requested product price' and denominator scope 'not a ratio - a currency amount reported per currency'.

A recomputation that yields counting the full value of the upgraded orders instead of the difference to the requested variant is detected as wrong: the stored aggregate and the independent recomputation must agree before the figure is published.
The dashboard payload for the same tenant and window carries the stored value with its window, coverage and measurement source; it substitutes neither a design target nor another metric's value.
Boundary behaviour: no upgrade in the window reports 0 TWD as a measured zero with window and coverage stated; missing source data is never rendered as a measured zero.
forbidden: Booking the full order value as upsell revenue.
Attributing the same difference to more than one order.
evidence: Order price-difference table per upgraded order.
Variant price list used to derive the difference.
cleanup: Delete gov- aggregate, raw-counter and scenario rows for SAL-04 after exporting the recomputation table.
automation: The reporting service and the metric dictionary run as real code under test over the frozen KPI dataset; the dashboard is a consumer whose displayed value must equal the independently recomputed value. Waits are condition-based on the stored aggregate row, metric values are never supplied as inputs, and no vendor boundary is involved in the arithmetic.
